title: Global stock markets slump as Anthropic's record IPO fails to stem AI sell-off
lede: Anthropic shares fell as much as 12% on their second trading day, sliding toward the $83 IPO price, as a broad AI sell-off hit chipmakers and Asian markets had their worst week since 2020.

points: The stock rose 17% on its debut after briefly jumping almost 40%, then dropped to $85.12 on Friday.
The Nasdaq lost 2%, with SanDisk down 14% and Micron 10%; Taiwan's market fell 6.7% and TSMC about 6%.
An IG analyst suggested the listing may be draining liquidity as investors sell other tech holdings to buy in.
Analysts say demand for AI exposure is strong, but valuations, profitability and the scale of AI spending are weighing on markets.
Nvidia fell 3% after California subpoenaed it over whether its chips ended up in China.

points.text: Several read a frontier lab going public as a signal that the market has peaked.
Others reply that IPOs usually underperform and high-beta stocks fall hardest in a sell-off, so the drop says little about Anthropic in particular.
One argues the price reflects open-weight models trailing by only months, which caps Anthropic's value even if AI succeeds.
A side thread asks whether automating high-wage industries shrinks GDP, with a reply arguing the savings get spent elsewhere.
